title: the documented fixed substrate port is unsafe on a shared host: a fresh agent on the CI box got 500s answered by OTHER agents' orphaned daemons
reasoning:
WHY (found live 2026-09-24, 5th dogfood run's ephemeral-bunker install leg)

The README's Quick start requires "a running DuckBrain on 127.0.0.1:3000" and the
Substrate pin section gives the boot line with no --port. On the CI box
(bunker-las-03, a multi-user rootless-Docker host) that assumption silently
breaks, in a way that produces a WRONG ERROR rather than a clear one.

Observed on a fresh agent (d1a530b6), following the docs verbatim:
  init -> could not list namespaces (500): {'error': "Cannot determine the
          duckbrain root: no duckbrain.config.json was found walking up from
          /home/bunker-864a37ab/duckbrain/src/config, ..."}

/home/bunker-864a37ab is a DIFFERENT, already-DESTROYED dogfood agent's home
directory. The box was holding four daemons at once: `kara`'s on :3000, and
orphans from destroyed agents 4b004b7a (started 00:48) and 864a37ab (Sep 22)
still bound to :3100/:3210/:3311 and still answering requests. Because the fresh
agent's own boot had silently failed to win a port (or the request simply reached
a stranger's listener), auger reported a 500 whose error text names a path that
no longer exists — the worst possible diagnostic.

Isolating on a verified-free port and pinning DUCKBRAIN_URL made the same
documented loop pass in 1 SECOND, so this is purely a port/addressing problem,
not an auger or substrate correctness problem.

DELIVERABLE
- README Substrate pin: give the boot line a non-default port for shared hosts
  (`node bin/duckbrain.js http --port 39xx`) and say WHY (a fixed 127.0.0.1:3000
  collides on any multi-user box, and another user's daemon will answer you);
  add the one-line port-free check (`ss -tlnp | grep <port>` or a connect probe)
  before starting, and the DUCKBRAIN_URL export that points auger at it
- diagnostics.md: record the failure signature — a 500 whose message names a
  home directory that is not yours means you reached someone else's substrate;
  the fix is domain separation by port, never killing the other daemon (you may
  not own it)
- optionally, auger itself should treat an unexpected 500 at init as this class
  and say so (a foreign-substrate hint when the error text names a path outside
  $HOME)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- the README documents a port-explicit boot line for shared hosts plus the
  DUCKBRAIN_URL pin, and a fresh agent following ONLY the docs reaches a stored
  decision (this run needed the undocumented isolation step)
- docs/dogfood/diagnostics.md carries the foreign-substrate failure signature
- no change requires touching another user's process, or any repo
  visibility/permission/clone setting
